BBVA puts AI agents’ controls to the test
sum: The bank’s new framework promises faster agent deployment and shorter software release cycles, making continuous evaluation, human oversight and operational resilience central to the next phase of its AI expansion.

BBVA is moving from individual artificial intelligence use cases towards a common framework for deploying agents across its business, setting out plans that put software assurance and operational controls at the centre of its expansion.
Unveiled on 6 October at a Strategic Talk with analysts and investors, the framework, called The Frame, is intended to standardise how the bank creates, deploys, manages and governs AI agents.
The announcement comes ahead of planned rollouts in 2027 across customer-facing services, relationship management and other banking functions.

For software testing and quality assurance teams, the significant development is the bank’s stated intention to combine faster deployment with defined agent permissions, operational boundaries and continuous performance evaluation.

As agents gain access to banking systems and take on more tasks, assurance will need to address both the quality of their outputs and the actions they are permitted to execute, according to Antonio Bravo, BBVA’s global head of AI transformation.
“‘The Frame’ will allow us to build many more agents, faster, in a way that is secure, repeatable and manageable, while maintaining control and creating value,” explained Bravo.

sum: - European stocks are looking more tentative to start the new week/month, although Spanish equities are enjoying some respite

European stocks are off to a rather subdued start to the new month, with most major indices observing light changes as the session gets underway. The cautious mood comes after a rough end to October as investors continue to grapple with concerns surrounding AI spending and the outlook for major central banks amid growing inflation pressures. Here are the opening changes:

After a miserable run last week, the IBEX is seen bouncing back a little and seeking a bit of a respite today. Spanish stocks had been battered by the fallout from Brazil's election shock, with banking heavyweights such as Santander and BBVA coming under significant selling pressure. The early gains today offer some welcome relief, although there's still plenty of ground to make up after the recent declines.
Besides that, there's not much appetite elsewhere across Europe. As things stand, investors are still trying to find their footing after last week's selloff in techn shares especially.

Even with the better mood in US futures today, we're not seeing that translate to any rebound in the broader risk mood. S&P 500 futures are up 0.3% with Nasdaq futures up 0.7% as tech shares lead the bounce for now. But again, it comes after a bloodbath on Friday as there remains plenty of questions surrounding lofty AI spending commitments and whether they will eventually translate into meaningful returns. And those won't be going away any time soon.

We'll still have a couple of big central bank decisions to deal with this week, with the RBA and BOE lined up. And on the economic data front, we will have Eurozone inflation data and the US jobs report on the cards too. But before we get to much of those items on the agenda, the US midterm elections tomorrow will be the bigger focus.
So, all of that should give traders plenty to chew on as November gets underway.

Garanti BBVA stock secures EUR 400 million in DPR financing
sum: Garanti BBVA has secured EUR 400 million in diversified payment rights financing, according to a BBVA announcement published on October 27, 2026. The transaction was arranged in international markets under the bank's foreign borrowing program and has maturities of 1,907 and 2,547 days.

The financing is structured through the bank's Diversified Payment Rights, or DPR, program. The structure is based on existing and future foreign-currency payment orders and is intended to diversify Garanti BBVA's wholesale funding sources while strengthening access to longer-term financing.

BBVA described the transaction as Garanti BBVA's first DPR financing since 2019. The bank's CEO Mahmut Akten said the transaction would diversify funding sources and strengthen international partnerships. Those statements describe management's strategic view and do not by themselves establish an effect on earnings or the share price.

Of the financing, EUR 50 million is designated for small and medium-sized businesses owned or managed by women. A further EUR 50 million is intended for micro, small and medium-sized businesses owned or managed by entrepreneurs under 35. BBVA said the programs are designed to support investment, growth and access to finance.

This pending corporate action has created short-term overhang on the equity, leading institutional investors to de-risk ahead of the offer outcome.

Beyond the M&A dynamics, sentiment is impacted by macroeconomic headwinds and currency volatility in BBVA's core growth regions, particularly Mexico and Turkey. Elevated interest rate uncertainty and foreign exchange fluctuations in these key international markets raise questions over near-term profit translation and credit quality. Though the bank continues to demonstrate solid underlying earnings power, exposure to volatile emerging market dynamics is prompting increased caution among market participants.

Surging fixed-income yields and general risk aversion have induced profit-taking across top-performing bank equities that recently traded near multi-year valuation peaks. Despite positive underlying corporate announcements—such as the recent approval of a record interim cash dividend and the ongoing execution of share repurchase programs—the current market environment favors capital preservation, driving near-term weakness in the stock.

items.t: Improve Your Retirement Income with These 3 Top-Ranked Dividend Stocks
sum: Believe it or not, seniors fear running out of cash more than they fear dying.

And unfortunately, even retirees who have built a nest egg have good reason to be concerned-with the traditional approaches to retirement planning, income may no longer cover expenses. That means retirees are dipping into principal to make ends meet, setting up a race against time between dwindling investment balances and longer lifespans.
Retirement investing approaches of the past don't work today.

For example, 10-year Treasury bonds in the late 1990s offered a yield of around 6.50%, which translated to an income source you could count on. However, today's yield is much lower and probably not a viable return option to fund typical retirements.
While this yield reduction may not seem drastic, it adds up: for a $1 million investment in 10-year Treasuries, the rate drop means a difference in yield of more than $1 million.

Today's retirees are getting hit hard by reduced bond yields-and the Social Security picture isn't too rosy either. Right now and for the near future, Social Security benefits are still being paid, but it has been estimated that the Social Security funds will be depleted as soon as 2035.

How can you avoid dipping into your principal when the investments you counted on in retirement aren't producing income? You can only cut your expenses so far, and the only other option is to find a different investment vehicle to generate income.

sum: The proven Zacks Rank system focuses on earnings estimates and estimate revisions to find winning stocks. Nevertheless, we know that our readers all have their own perspectives, so we are always looking at the latest trends in value, growth, and momentum to find strong picks.

Looking at the history of these trends, perhaps none is more beloved than value investing. This strategy simply looks to identify companies that are being undervalued by the broader market. Value investors use fundamental analysis and traditional valuation metrics to find stocks that they believe are being undervalued by the market at large.

Luckily, Zacks has developed its own Style Scores system in an effort to find stocks with specific traits. Value investors will be interested in the system's "Value" category. Stocks with both "A" grades in the Value category and high Zacks Ranks are among the strongest value stocks on the market right now.

One company to watch right now is Banco Bilbao Viscaya Argentaria (BBVA). BBVA is currently holding a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) and a Value grade of A. The stock holds a P/E ratio of 9.5, while its industry has an average P/E of 10.76. Over the last 12 months, BBVA's Forward P/E has been as high as 9.83 and as low as 5.63, with a median of 7.70.

We should also highlight that BBVA has a P/B ratio of 1.63. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. This stock's P/B looks attractive against its industry's average P/B of 2.72. Within the past 52 weeks, BBVA's P/B has been as high as 1.63 and as low as 0.85, with a median of 1.24.

Finally, our model also underscores that BBVA has a P/CF ratio of 8.79. This metric takes into account a company's operating cash flow and can be used to find stocks that are undervalued based on their solid cash outlook. BBVA's current P/CF looks attractive when compared to its industry's average P/CF of 18.45. Within the past 12 months, BBVA's P/CF has been as high as 8.79 and as low as 4.56, with a median of 6.19.
These figures are just a handful of the metrics value investors tend to look at, but they help show that Banco Bilbao Viscaya Argentaria is likely being undervalued right now.
